description:
FILED s446l (agent L) from #502 probes; PRE-EXISTING, cosmetic-looking but a
wrong VALUE.

REPRO: `print "[$:]\n";` -- perl prints `[ \n-]` (space, NEWLINE, hyphen: the
three characters format/write may break a line on).  PCL prints `[ n-]`: a
literal lower-case n where the newline should be.  Found while probing every
punctuation variable for #502 (s446l); it was the only DEFAULT-VALUE mismatch
among the 45 names -- everything else agreed.

The shape of the bug says an escape was lost when the default was written:
look for the defvar of |$:| in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp and check whether the
initial string is " \n-" (correct) or " n-" (a CL string in which the
backslash was consumed or never written).

It matters where format/write actually breaks lines (docs/not-supported.md has
`format`/`write` as absent, so the consumer may be absent too) -- but the
VALUE is readable by any program and is wrong today, and the fix is one
character.

BAR: `print "[$:]"` vs perl; the assignment path ($: = "x") unchanged; cl/
change so a full sweep, though no corpus file is expected to read it.


DONE s448o (Opus, agent O of round 6), commit 97b10b6 (rebased).

The task's suspicion was exactly right, and the mechanism is worth writing down
because it will happen again: the defvar DID read `(make-p-box " \n-")` in the
source.  A CL string literal has NO \n escape -- the reader takes a backslash as
"the next character, literally" -- so those five source characters are the THREE
characters space, letter n, hyphen.  Spelled now the way |$/| spells its own
default: `(concatenate 'string " " (string #\Newline) "-")`.

SCANNED FOR SIBLINGS: every string literal in cl/*.lisp, looking for a
backslash before an alphanumeric (a little parser that skips ;-comments and
#\char literals -- a plain grep drowns in docstrings).  cl/pcl-runtime.lisp has
exactly one hit, this one; every other hit in the tree is a properly-doubled
`\\` in a regex source, or descriptive text in cl/skip-registry.lisp.  So it is
a single slip, not a family.

Guard Pl/t/caret-vars-01.t row 6, which compares the ORDS rather than the
rendering -- printing " \n-" straight would compare a literal newline and hide a
one-character slip.
subject: $: (FORMAT_LINE_BREAK_CHARACTERS) defaults to " n-" where perl has " \n-" -- a lost backslash-n in the runtime's initial value
